# Conserved synteny across Kiritimatiellia


::: {.paper-links}
[Preprint: Oliver, Podell & Allen 2026, *bioRxiv*](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.06.756941)
[Code: KiritimatiallesSCoNe](https://github.com/AaronAOliver/KiritimatiallesSCoNe)
:::

Kiritimatiellia are a class of Verrucomicrobiota. The few cultured members
carry very large sets of carbohydrate-active enzymes and sulfatases, but most
families in the class are known only from metagenome-assembled genomes, and
their genome organization has not been described.

To compare gene neighborhoods across 898 genomes, I built a new data structure:
the similarity-colocalization network (SCoNe). It merges homologous proteins
into communities, then links communities that repeatedly sit in the same gene
neighborhoods, so conserved synteny shows up as heavy edges. This notebook
builds a SCoNe from a synthetic dataset, then shows the networks from the real
data.

```{python}
import sys, itertools, collections, random
random.seed(42)          # igraph draws from Python's RNG: fixes Leiden + layouts
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import igraph as ig
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import plotly.express as px
from _common import repo_path, show

REPO = repo_path("KiritimatiallesSCoNe")
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))
from scone.scone_metrics import ari, sea, coloc_modularity   # metrics straight from the SCoNe package
```

## How a SCoNe is built

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 5
flowchart TB
  P[Proteins<br/>all-vs-all DIAMOND] --> S[Sequence similarity<br/>network]
  S --> L[Weighted Leiden<br/>homology communities]
  N[Gene neighborhoods<br/>dbCAN CGCs, antiSMASH BGCs<br/>Spacedust synteny, flanking genes] --> C
  L --> C[Count community pairs<br/>that share a neighborhood]
  C --> X[SCoNe<br/>nodes = communities<br/>edges = conserved colocalization]
```

The tool reads the neighborhoods as input rather than inferring them. The same
code can therefore work on dbCAN gene clusters, antiSMASH regions, Spacedust
synteny blocks, or the genes around one query gene.

### Step 1: a sequence similarity network

The synthetic dataset from Figure 2.1 has 712 proteins from 30 planted families,
spread across 22 gene clusters. All-vs-all DIAMOND hits with an E-value of
10<sup>-10</sup> or lower are kept, and each edge is weighted by
-log<sub>10</sub>(E-value), as in `build_ssn_leiden.py`.

```{python}
mock = REPO / "examples" / "mock"
cols = ["q", "s", "pident", "len", "mm", "gap", "qs", "qe", "ss", "se", "evalue", "bits"]
hits = pd.read_csv(mock / "diamond.tsv", sep="\t", names=cols)
hits = hits[(hits.q != hits.s) & (hits.evalue <= 1e-10)].copy()
hits["a"] = hits[["q", "s"]].min(axis=1)
hits["b"] = hits[["q", "s"]].max(axis=1)
edges = (hits.groupby(["a", "b"], as_index=False)["evalue"].min()
             .assign(weight=lambda d: -np.log10(d.evalue.clip(lower=1e-300))))

nodes = pd.read_csv(mock / "nodes.txt", header=None)[0].tolist()
truth = pd.read_csv(mock / "annotations.tsv", sep="\t").set_index("protein_id")["gene"]

g = ig.Graph()
g.add_vertices(nodes)
g.add_edges(list(zip(edges.a, edges.b)))
g.es["weight"] = edges.weight.tolist()
print(f"{g.vcount()} proteins, {g.ecount():,} similarity edges")
```

### Step 2: homology communities with weighted Leiden

```{python}
part = g.community_leiden(objective_function="modularity", weights="weight",
                          resolution=1.0, n_iterations=-1)
leiden = dict(zip(nodes, part.membership))
fam = [truth.get(n, "none") for n in nodes]
print(f"{len(part)} Leiden communities; "
      f"ARI vs. planted families = {ari(part.membership, fam):.3f}")
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "The mock SSN colored by Leiden community. Hover over a node to see its planted family. Some families split into several communities, which the SCoNe step then handles."
layout = g.layout_fruchterman_reingold(weights=[np.log1p(w) for w in g.es["weight"]], niter=500, seed=None)
xy = np.array(layout.coords)
ex, ey = [], []
for e in g.es.select(lambda e: e.index % 3 == 0):         # draw every third edge to keep the figure light
    s, t = e.tuple
    ex += [xy[s, 0], xy[t, 0], None]; ey += [xy[s, 1], xy[t, 1], None]
palette = px.colors.qualitative.Dark24 + px.colors.qualitative.Light24
fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Scattergl(x=ex, y=ey, mode="lines", line=dict(width=.4, color="#5a6272"),
                           hoverinfo="skip", showlegend=False))
fig.add_trace(go.Scattergl(
    x=xy[:, 0], y=xy[:, 1], mode="markers",
    marker=dict(size=8, color=[palette[m % len(palette)] for m in part.membership],
                line=dict(width=.3, color="#111")),
    text=[f"{n}<br>planted family: {f}<br>Leiden community {m}" for n, f, m in zip(nodes, fam, part.membership)],
    hoverinfo="text", showlegend=False))
fig.update_layout(height=430, margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=10, b=10),
                  xaxis=dict(visible=False), yaxis=dict(visible=False))
show(fig)
```

### Step 3: collapse communities and add colocalization edges

Each gene cluster adds 1 to the weight of every pair of communities it contains, counted
once per neighborhood. Edge weight is therefore the number of independent
neighborhoods in which two homology groups appear together.

```{python}
cmap = pd.read_csv(mock / "cluster_genome_map.tsv", sep="\t")
comm_size = collections.Counter(part.membership)
co = collections.Counter()
for genes in cmap.genes:
    comms = sorted({leiden[x] for x in genes.split(",") if x in leiden})
    co.update(itertools.combinations(comms, 2))

# label each community by its majority planted family (>= 75%), else auxiliary_N
labels = {}
for c in comm_size:
    members = [truth.get(n, "none") for n in nodes if leiden[n] == c]
    top, k = collections.Counter(members).most_common(1)[0]
    labels[c] = top if k / len(members) >= .75 else f"auxiliary_{c}"

sc = ig.Graph()
sc.add_vertices(sorted(comm_size))
sc.add_edges([(a, b) for a, b in co])
sc.es["weight"] = list(co.values())
print(f"SCoNe: {sc.vcount()} community nodes, {sc.ecount()} colocalization edges "
      f"(max weight {max(co.values())})")
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "The mock SCoNe. Node size follows community size (12 + 5.25 times the square root of n, as in the tool). Edge width and opacity follow how many gene clusters share the pair. Hover over a node to see its family."
pos = np.array(sc.layout_kamada_kawai().coords)   # spreads the dense block more evenly than FR
fig = go.Figure()
wmax = max(sc.es["weight"])
for e in sc.es:
    s, t = e.tuple; w = e["weight"]
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=[pos[s, 0], pos[t, 0]], y=[pos[s, 1], pos[t, 1]], mode="lines",
                             line=dict(width=.5 + 5 * w / wmax, color=f"rgba(140,210,213,{.15 + .75 * w / wmax:.2f})"),
                             hoverinfo="text", text=f"{labels[s]} and {labels[t]}: {w} clusters", showlegend=False))
vids = list(range(sc.vcount()))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=pos[:, 0], y=pos[:, 1], mode="markers+text",
    marker=dict(size=[(12 + 5.25 * np.sqrt(comm_size[v])) / 1.6 for v in vids],
                color=[palette[v % len(palette)] for v in vids], line=dict(width=1, color="#111")),
    text=[labels[v] for v in vids], textposition="top center", textfont=dict(size=10, color="#eaeaea"),
    hovertext=[f"<b>{labels[v]}</b><br>{comm_size[v]} proteins<br>degree {sc.degree(v)}" for v in vids],
    hoverinfo="text", showlegend=False))
fig.update_layout(height=480, margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=10, b=10),
                  xaxis=dict(visible=False), yaxis=dict(visible=False))
show(fig)
```

### Scoring a SCoNe

`scone_metrics.py` defines SCoNe Edge Agreement (SEA). It is an adjusted
Rand index computed over the colocalization edges rather than over genes, so it
only penalizes partition differences that change the network's wiring. The
package also defines colocalization modularity, which measures how well a partition lines
up communities with the block structure of the neighborhoods.

```{python}
coloc_edges = set()
for genes in cmap.genes:
    coloc_edges.update(itertools.combinations(sorted(x for x in genes.split(",") if x), 2))
p_leiden = {n: str(leiden[n]) for n in nodes}
p_truth = {n: truth.get(n, "none") for n in nodes}
p_singletons = {n: n for n in nodes}
pd.DataFrame({
    "Partition": ["Weighted Leiden", "Planted families", "Every protein alone"],
    "SEA vs. planted": [sea(coloc_edges, p_leiden, p_truth), 1.0, sea(coloc_edges, p_singletons, p_truth)],
    "Colocalization modularity": [coloc_modularity(coloc_edges, p) for p in (p_leiden, p_truth, p_singletons)],
}).style.hide(axis="index").format(precision=3)
```

## A survey of 898 genomes

```{python}
meta = pd.read_csv(REPO / "data" / "metadata" / "tree_metadata.tsv", sep="\t")
src = pd.read_csv(REPO / "data" / "metadata" / "gtdb_genome_source.tsv", sep="\t")
meta = meta.merge(src, left_on="accession", right_on="Accession", how="left")
cat_colors = {"Host-Associated": "#ee5f5b", "Aquatic & Sediment": "#52adc8",
              "Wastewater & Built Environment": "#f89406", "Terrestrial": "#62c462", "Unknown": "#6b7588"}
order = ["Unknown", "Terrestrial", "Wastewater & Built Environment", "Aquatic & Sediment", "Host-Associated"]
meta = meta.assign(_o=meta.category.map(order.index)).sort_values("_o")   # Unknown drawn first, underneath
fig = px.scatter(meta, x="cazyme_pct", y="sulfatase_pct", color="category", color_discrete_map=cat_colors,
                 category_orders={"category": order[::-1]},
                 size="cds_count", size_max=14, opacity=.8,
                 hover_data={"accession": True, "isolation_source": True, "Genome Source": True,
                             "cazyme_count": True, "sulfatase_count": True, "cds_count": False},
                 labels={"cazyme_pct": "CAZymes (% of CDS)", "sulfatase_pct": "Sulfatases (% of CDS)",
                         "category": "Isolation source"})
fig.update_layout(height=500, legend=dict(itemsizing="constant"))
show(fig)
```

Point size is the number of coding sequences (CDS) in the genome.
Host-associated genomes devote the largest share of their genes to CAZymes
(median 2.9% of CDS). Sulfatases are mostly an aquatic trait: the median
aquatic or sediment genome encodes sulfatases at 0.4% of its CDS, while the
median host-associated genome encodes none. Across genomes, CAZyme and
sulfatase counts are only weakly correlated (Spearman's rho = 0.18).

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Median number of genes per genome in each polysaccharide-target class, by isolation source."
cls = pd.read_csv(REPO / "data" / "metadata" / "cazyme_class_counts.tsv", sep="\t")
heat = (cls.merge(meta[["genome", "category"]], on="genome")
           .groupby("category").median(numeric_only=True)
           .loc[["Host-Associated", "Aquatic & Sediment", "Wastewater & Built Environment", "Terrestrial", "Unknown"]])
fig = go.Figure(go.Heatmap(z=heat.values, x=heat.columns, y=heat.index, colorscale="Teal",
                           hovertemplate="%{y}<br>%{x}: %{z} genes<extra></extra>",
                           text=heat.values, texttemplate="%{text:.0f}", colorbar=dict(title="genes")))
fig.update_layout(height=400, xaxis_tickangle=-45, margin=dict(l=190, b=130), yaxis_autorange="reversed")
show(fig)
```

## Beyond glycans: hydrogenases, nitrogen fixation, natural products

The same SCoNe approach was applied to genes flanking [FeFe]-hydrogenases, to
*nif* loci, and to aryl-polyene and other biosynthetic gene clusters. The
results suggest that sulfated glycan hydrolysis fuels fermentation,
hydrogenases balance redox, and surplus carbon supports nitrogen fixation.

```{python}
hyd = pd.read_csv(REPO / "data" / "hyd" / "hyddb_run" / "hydA_hyddb_classification.tsv", sep="\t")
hyd["organisation"] = hyd.organisation.str.replace("_", " ")
hyd["HydDB_FeFe_subtype"] = hyd.HydDB_FeFe_subtype.str.replace("_", " ")
tab = hyd.groupby(["HydDB_FeFe_subtype", "organisation"]).size().reset_index(name="n")
order = hyd.HydDB_FeFe_subtype.value_counts().index.tolist()
fig = px.bar(tab, x="HydDB_FeFe_subtype", y="n", color="organisation", category_orders={"HydDB_FeFe_subtype": order},
             labels={"HydDB_FeFe_subtype": "HydDB [FeFe] subtype", "n": "hydA genes", "organisation": "Locus organization"})
fig.update_layout(height=380, barmode="stack",
                  title=dict(text=f"{len(hyd):,} [FeFe]-hydrogenase catalytic subunits in {hyd.genome.nunique()} genomes",
                             font=dict(size=13)))
show(fig)
```

```{python}
bgc = pd.read_csv(REPO / "data" / "aryl_bgc" / "community_meta.tsv", sep="\t")
top = bgc.sort_values("size", ascending=False).head(25).copy()
# label each community by its most common Pfam domain
top["label"] = top.dom_pfam.replace("-", "no Pfam") + " (" + top.community.str.replace("auxiliary_", "#") + ")"
fig = px.bar(top, x="size", y="label", color="dom_gene_kind", orientation="h",
             category_orders={"label": top.label.tolist()},
             hover_data=["n_gcfs", "dom_pfam", "pfam_frac"],
             labels={"size": "proteins in community", "label": "", "dom_gene_kind": "Dominant gene kind"})
fig.update_layout(height=600, title=dict(text="Largest homology communities in BGC neighborhoods", font=dict(size=13)))
show(fig)
```

## Running SCoNe on other data

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/AaronAOliver/KiritimatiallesSCoNe
diamond blastp -q proteins.faa -d db -o hits.tsv --outfmt 6 --max-target-seqs 3000 -e 1e-3
scone run --homology hits.tsv --coloc neighborhoods.tsv --annotations annotations.tsv \
          --evalue 1e-30 --min-cluster-size 3 --min-edge-weight 5 --out-prefix out/run1 --cyjs
```

`neighborhoods.tsv` has one row per neighborhood (`cluster_id`, `genome`, and
a comma-separated list of `genes`). The output is an interactive HTML SSN and
SCoNe, the community table, SVGs, and a `.cyjs` file for Cytoscape desktop.
